title: Quickpatch Conductor — idempotent one-click admin fixes with safety harness
creator: Aisha Rana
description:
Problem: On-call engineers frequently perform small, repeatable remedial actions (eg. restart a worker, rotate a cache key, clear a prefetched prefix) that are safety-sensitive and error-prone. We need a curated ‘one-click’ operator that executes idempotent remediation steps with automated dry-run, approval gating, telemetry, and rollback so junior oncall or SREs can safely apply fixes without writing ad-hoc scripts.

Goal: Build Quickpatch Conductor — a lightweight control plane that converts vetted runbook steps into parameterized, idempotent tasks that can be executed from Console or CLI. Tasks should support: dry-run, strict RBAC, staged rollout (canary -> global), pre-check and post-check probes, automatic rollback on failed post-checks, and end-to-end telemetry for success/failure/cost.

Non-goals: replace full runbook DSL or complex multi-step incident automation (we integrate with existing runbook orchestrator later). This is for single-step or small atomic remediation operations.

Acceptance criteria:
- UI + CLI to select a Quickpatch and supply parameters, run in dry-run mode, and view simulated changes.
- Execution path enforces idempotency and pre/post probes; failures trigger rollback and emit structured telemetry.
- Run history recorded with operator, parameters, logs, and trace links; searchable in Console.
- RBAC policies via existing SSO/KMS integration; only authorized roles can promote from dry-run to live.
- Unit/integration tests + canary rollout to staging and one production shard.

Design notes:
- Quickpatches stored as parameterized Runbook fragments (YAML templates) with a small shim that wraps execution in: precheck -> dry-run-sim -> gated approve -> exec -> postcheck -> commit/rollback.
- Enforce idempotency by requiring a reversible marker (eg. generated transaction id + compensating action) or using provider-API idempotency tokens.
- Telemetry: emit events for start/finish/result/error/retry/rollback with context (model, region, instance, operator). Hook into Ops Console traces and cost dashboards.
- Safety harness: dry-run must be available by default; to execute live user must have ‘quickpatch.apply’ scope and a secondary approval if action touches dedicated capacity or private deployment resources.
- Observability: attach traces to existing request IDs where applicable; surface per-patch SLA (mean time to repair, success rate).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec Quickpatch schema and validator (2d).
2) Build shim that wraps existing runbook step executor (3d).
3) Add dry-run simulation layer and pre/post probe hooks (3d).
4) Integrate RBAC and approval gating in Console + CLI (4d).
5) Telemetry + logs + searchable history (3d).
6) End-to-end tests + staging canary + rollout (5d).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: a poorly defined patch could cause broad impact. Mitigation: require mandatory pre/post probes and a sandbox verification step before registering a Quickpatch.
- Risk: operators bypass dry-run. Mitigation: enforce scope checks and log/alert on bypass attempts.
- Risk: rollback complexity for external systems. Mitigation: require compensating action or API idempotency support when onboarding patches, disallow unsafe actions in first iteration.

Notes for reviewers: look for missing failure modes and proposed telemetry schema that covers recovery steps.
